title: Nothing tells us which items are late
description:
Write the test first. This ticket is deliberately test-first: add the failing test to tests/test_store.py, watch it fail, then make it pass.

tinytodo/store.py defines `Store` with `add(title, due=None)` (line 10), `complete` (line 16) and `all` (line 22). `due` is a day number (an int) counted from day 0, or None for "no due date". Add `overdue(self, today)` to `Store`, directly after `all()`.

It returns the list of item dicts (the same `{"id", "title", "done", "due"}` dicts `all()` returns) that are LATE, in insertion order. An item is late when its `due` is an int STRICTLY LESS THAN `today`. An item due exactly on `today` is not late. An item whose `due` is None is never late. An item whose `done` is True is never late, whatever its due day. Nothing late returns an empty list.

Add tests for each of those five rules to tests/test_store.py before you implement `overdue`. Do not change `add`, `complete` or `all`, and every test already in tests/test_store.py must still pass unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_store.py gains a test per rule, written before the fix
an item is late only when due is an int strictly less than today
an item due exactly today, or with due None, is never late
a completed item is never late whatever its due day
it returns whole item dicts in insertion order, [] when none are late
every test already in tests/test_store.py still passes, unchanged
